existing_roles.title: Quality Improvement Director
existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

Contentnea Health is a Community Health Center providing comprehensive medical, dental and behavioral health services for members of our communities in Greene, Pitt and Pamlico counties in eastern North Carolina.

**Job Summary**

Provides strategic leadership, oversight, and coordination of all organizational quality initiatives, including designing, implementing and evaluating quality programs to ensure delivery of safe, patient-centered, equitable, and efficient care, leads data-driven improvement efforts, and supports regulatory reporting and compliance with standards.

**Responsibilities and Duties**

* Oversees the Quality Improvement (QI) department activities.
 + Leads the development, implementation, and evaluation of the organization’s Quality Improvement Program.
 + Identifies opportunities to support QI efforts through evaluation, testing, and/or integration for electronic health record (EHR) functionality and other Heath Information and Technology (HIT) systems.
 + Summarizes and shares clinical quality data with the Board, key leadership, and staff to inform decision-making and priorities for improvement.
 + Champions the adoption of standardized best practices and lessons learned across disciplines and departments at the care team level and at the organizational level using communication tools, published workflows, staff meetings, events and trainings.
 + Facilitates QI Committee meetings and ensures documentation, follow-up, and progress tracking.
 + Establishes annual QI goals, work plans, and performance benchmarks aligned with strategic priorities.
 + Develops dashboards and data tools to share performance results with leadership and staff.
* Collaborates with and guides clinical care team members to establish QI processes through the organization.
 + Leads or participates in work teams related to QI and functions as a coach to support care team in building, fostering patient-centeredness and healthy patient outcomes.
 + Researches external organizations and participates in training opportunities, and works with partners, consultants and experts to guide QI efforts.
 + Assesses the need for and facilitates education, training, and technical assistance for staff to ensure compliance with QI efforts.
 + Uses existing data systems to identify areas in need of quality improvement across the organization.
* Oversees organizational data submission and sharing to external entities in collaboration with other departments as needed.
 + Follows regulation on data collection and reporting structure as defined by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and health plan incentives.
 + Approaches changes to the EHR or other IT systems with consideration to data governance.
 + Monitors Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) requirements and the health center’s compliance.
 + Leads the annual FTCA deeming and redeeming application process and ensures all required evidence and documentation are completed and submitted accurately.
 + Ensures accurate and timely reporting of UDS clinical measures and other federal/state quality requirements.
 + Participates in HRSA review and response with organization leaders.
 + Acts as administrator for electronic Value-Based Care (VBC) and Quality Incentive Plans (QIP) platforms.
 + Partners with key leadership to determine participation priorities.
 + Oversees QI and clinical participation in contracted VBC and QIPs.
 + Monitors performance with VBC and incentive plans; shares performance data with key leadership.
* Ensures ongoing alignment with Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) standards, manages The National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) reporting and serves as PCMH project manager.
 + Leads annual submission of PCMH report to maintain recognition for each recognized site and maintains documentation and policies needed for audits, accreditation, and regulatory compliance.
 + Ensures all new hires are trained in PCMH processes, policies, and workflows, including care coordination, team-based care, access, patient experience and satisfaction.
 + Maintains current knowledge of NCQA/PCMH standards and serves as the subject matter expert. Analyzes and reviews processes, policies, and systems on an ongoing basis to ensure they are aligned with current and updated PCMH standards.
 + Uses data to drive continuous improvement in clinical quality, patient experience and cost/utilization outcomes.
 + Reports PCMH performance to leadership to inform resource allocation and prioritize performance improvement activities.
 + Coordinates PCMH improvement activities with staff and leadership.
* Provides overall management and direction to departmental staff.
 + Oversees the development and maintenance of the departmental budget; monitors ongoing budgetary compliance and addresses problems as needed.
 + Delegates departmental duties and responsibilities; participates in high priority special projects and activities.
 + Represents the department at all senior management meetings.
 + Prepares departmental company policies and procedures and conveys all senior management communications and directives.
 + Monitors departmental performance using company performance standards and addresses issues as needed.
 + Directs departmental performance and provides specific instructions on completion of tasks/responsibilities.
 + Prepares and conducts performance appraisals for immediate staff.
 + Conducts hiring, disciplinary, and termination procedures.

**Qualifications and Skills**

Bachelor Degree in Nursing. Current licensure as a Registered Nurse in good standing with the NC Board of Nursing. Possesses advanced understanding of quality improvement theory and quality methodology, evidence-based practice, state and national priorities for patient safety and population health as determined by HRSA, DHHS, and other entities, and regulatory, recognition and compliance standards, such as FTCA, PCMH, and HRSA. The ideal candidate will have progressive experience in leading quality improvement activities and in leading staff.

existing_roles.title: Quality Director
existing_roles.description:
Description:

Exalt Health, an acute rehabilitation hospital, provides an intensive rehabilitation program, and admitted patients must be able to tolerate three hours of intense rehabilitation services per day. Focused on caring for patients with complex rehabilitative needs such as stroke, spinal cord injury, brain injury, head trauma, medically debilitation conditions, neurological disorders, cardio-pulmonary amputations, orthopedic injuries, and multiple major traumas.

**Position Summary**

The Quality Director is responsible for spearheading the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of a comprehensive quality and patient safety program throughout our inpatient rehabilitation hospital network. In this role, you will drive a culture of excellence, ensuring our delivery of the highest standards of patient care across all our facilities in Texas. This position demands strong leadership, data analysis skills, exceptional attention to detail, and an unwavering commitment to patient-centered care.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Strategic Planning: Design and implement a system-wide quality management framework, aligning with organizational goals and regulatory requirements.
* Performance Monitoring: Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of key quality metrics and patient outcome data. Identify trends, pinpoint areas for improvement, and develop targeted interventions.
* Continuous Improvement: Lead initiatives to enhance clinical quality, patient safety, and process efficiency across all rehabilitation facilities. Implement evidence-based best practices and drive innovation in quality improvement endeavors.
* Regulatory Compliance: Ensure adherence to all state, federal, and accreditation standards (e.g., The Joint Commission) related to quality management and patient safety.
* Education and Training: Develop and deliver educational programs to cultivate a quality-focused culture among staff at all levels.
* Collaboration: Partner with clinical leaders, department heads, and frontline staff to foster a collaborative environment focused on continuous improvement and patient satisfaction.
* Risk Management: Proactively identify and mitigate potential risks to patient safety and guide the organization in proactive risk management practices.
* Board Reporting: Prepare regular reports for the Executive Leadership team and Board of Directors, showcasing quality performance metrics, initiatives, and strategic recommendations.

Requirements:

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

Licenses or Certifications

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) or other relevant quality certifications highly desired.
* Current, unencumbered clinical licenses in the state where the hospital is operating required.

Education, Training, and Experience

* Education in a healthcare-related field or a clinical degree preferred.
* Minimum of 7-10 years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare quality management, with a proven track record in an inpatient hospital setting.

Skills and Abilities, Proficiency and Productivity Standards

* Deep knowledge of quality improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, PDSA).
* Expertise in healthcare regulatory standards, accreditation requirements, and best practices.
* Proficiency in healthcare data management and statistical analysis tools.
* Organizes and prioritizes tasks and projects, accurately completing job responsibilities within the specified time constraints.
* Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
* Analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to work under deadlines and handle multiple tasks.
* Speaks and communicates English effectively in verbal and written format; writes legibly.

existing_roles.title: Quality Assurance Director
existing_roles.description:
Arrowhead Winch engineers and manufactures industrial winch, hoist and drive systems under the BRADEN, CARCO and Gearmatic brand names in Broken Arrow and Okmulgee, Oklahoma. We are seeking a talented **Quality Assurance Director** to join our team in **Broken Arrow, Oklahoma.** Please note: This is a **100% on site** office-based position supporting both the Okmulgee and Broken Arrow, Oklahoma manufacturing plants. Benefits include 401K with matching up to 5%, plus profit sharing plan; medical, dental and vision plans; flexible spending and health savings accounts; paid short- and long-term disability program; paid life insurance; and paid holidays, sick and vacation time. Our work environments are clean, climate controlled and safe. Arrowhead Winch does require applicants to complete a background check, drug test, and pre-employment physical as a condition of employment. Our goal is for all employees to work safely without injury while maintaining the highest safety standards in compliance with company policies.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Position Overview:**

The Quality Assurance Director leads the Quality Department and builds a world-class, prevention-focused quality culture across the Broken Arrow and Okmulgee plants. Partnering with Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and frontline teams, this leader promotes quality at the source, shared accountability, and measurable customer satisfaction. The role oversees the ISO 9001 Quality Management System (QMS), customer and supplier quality, corrective action, measurement systems, traceability, warranty analysis, and new-product readiness.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Essential Functions/Responsibilities:**

* Build a quality-at-the-source culture through visible shop-floor leadership, employee engagement, supervisor coaching, recognition, and shared accountability.
* Set quality strategy and annual goals aligned with business priorities, customer requirements, and measurable results.
* Lead and standardize quality procedures, controls, audits, and ISO 9001 management reviews across both plants; ensure actions are completed and effective.
* Partner with Operations to strengthen standard work, in-process checks, visual controls, and mistake-proofing to prevent defects and improve first-pass yield.
* Establish clear expectations for employees to identify, contain, and escalate suspect product; support prompt action on quality concerns.
* Define quality standards and process controls for machining, welding, painting, assembly, and final testing.
* Track and review leading and lagging quality measures, including first-pass yield, customer escapes, scrap, rework, warranty cost, supplier rejects, cost of poor quality, and corrective-action effectiveness; assign owners for improvements.
* Monitor customer scorecards and ensure customer-specific specifications, certifications, inspection records, and corrective-action requirements are met at both plants.
* Communicate quality issues, containment plans, corrective actions, and verified closure promptly and accurately to customers.
* Develop employee quality awareness and problem-solving skills; maintain inspector training, qualification, and competency requirements.
* Lead Quality Department staffing, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and professional development.
* Oversee calibration, measurement system suitability, and gage repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) studies.
* Lead cross-functional root-cause analysis and corrective action using structured methods such as 8D or 5 Whys; verify actions prevent recurrence.
* Use risk-based and layered process audits to confirm compliance with critical controls and sustain improvements.
* Manage nonconforming material, including identification, containment, segregation, documented disposition, controlled deviations, and release authorization.
* Control process changes through risk assessment, approval, validation, documentation, and communication.
* Partner with Purchasing to improve supplier quality through scorecards, reject trends, audits or visits, and targeted corrective actions.
* Lead returned-product, warranty, and field-failure investigations; coordinate containment, customer feedback, and prevention of repeat issues.
* Partner with Design Engineering to improve manufacturability and eliminate design-related quality risks.
* Support new products, engineering changes, and process transfers through risk-based quality planning, PFMEAs, control plans, inspections, and process validation.
* Set end-of-line testing requirements and records; ensure failed tests are investigated and authorized before retest or product release.
* Maintain part, component, production, and test traceability appropriate to product and customer requirements.
* Manage the quality budget and prioritize sustainable improvements that reduce the cost of poor quality without compromising conformance.
* Manage customer specific process approvals, create qualification plans, and maintain required test results and certifications. Establish required internal processes that must be maintained to hold the customer certifications.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing, or a related field.
* Seven to ten years of quality leadership in ISO 9001 manufacturing, including machining and assembly, multi-site supervision, and team development.
* Proven success building a quality-first culture, coaching frontline teams, and reducing recurring defects through prevention and accountability.
* Ability to interpret part and assembly drawings; working knowledge of metrology and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).
* Practical experience with Lean/Six Sigma, structured root-cause analysis, and corrective-action effectiveness verification.
* Experience with statistical process control (SPC), Gage R&R, process capability, PFMEA, and control plans, including methods suited to low-volume, high-mix production.
* Strong analytical, technical, leadership, communication, and conflict-resolution skills; ability to influence cross-functional teams and work effectively with customers.
* Strong documentation and organizational skills; proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or Black Belt preferred).
* ISO 9001 Lead Auditor training or certification.
* Experience using short-run SPC, layered process audits, and mistake-proofing in low-volume, high-mix manufacturing.
* Welding inspection knowledge; AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) a plus.
* Knowledge of paint and coatings inspection.
* Knowledge and Experience using AI Tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot

**Physical Demands and Work Environment:**

* Sit, stand, and walk for extended periods, including in a manufacturing shop.
* Use a computer and review technical documents for extended periods.
* Have adequate vision to inspect parts and review documents.
* Hear and speak clearly for effective communication.
* Occasionally lift up to 50 lbs. with assistance and bend, squat, or stoop.
* Work around electrical and heavy equipment; handle and inspect parts.
* Wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) in applicable areas.
* Travel regularly between the Broken Arrow and Okmulgee plants.

Arrowhead provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, military and/or veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws in accordance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended, and the Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, which require affirmative action to ensure equal opportunity in all aspects of employment. If accommodation required, contact HR at 918-259-3259.

existing_roles.title: Director, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is hiring a Director of Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Quality to build and lead the team responsible for the technical relationship with our supplier base, from first sketch through high-volume production, and for the quality systems that ensure everything that arrives at our factories meets spec. This role reports into our VP, Global Supply Chain and brings together two functions that have to move as one: the engineers who industrialize our components and equipment, and the quality systems and team that hold our suppliers accountable once they are producing.

Form's 85% domestically sourced supply chain was built for a battery chemistry with no existing supplier base, which means the industrialization playbook and the quality systems we need are still being written. You will set that standard: rigorous enough to protect a product with a 100-hour duration promise, and practical enough to work with suppliers who are learning our process alongside us. You will fly high enough to set the strategy and the org, and go deep enough to sit in a root cause review when it matters. 
 
*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Lead Form's Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Supplier Quality organization, growing a team of engineers embedded across battery materials, components, and equipment categories.
* Own the end-to-end industrialization journey for direct materials and made-to-spec components, from design-for-manufacturability review and supplier selection through tooling qualification and sustaining production support.
* Build and own Form's supplier quality management system, including PPAP, APQP, PFMEA, control plans, and SCAR/8D corrective action processes, calibrated for a novel battery chemistry with no legacy supply base to borrow from.
* Set the technical bar for supplier selection and qualification, partnering with Global Supply Managers to ensure our sourcing strategy is backed by suppliers who can deliver on cost, quality, and schedule.
* Own supplier process capability and yield performance, coordinating with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, and Reliability teams to drive root cause analysis and corrective action when issues surface.
* Develop the roadmap and staffing plan for quality systems aligned to relevant standards (e.g., ISO 9001, IATF 16949) at a scale and stage appropriate to where Form is today and where we are headed.
* Represent supplier technical and quality readiness within the Product Development Process, ensuring every component and supplier is qualified ahead of commercial scale.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to align supplier roadmaps with Form's build plan and deployment targets.

### **What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 12+ years of experience in supplier industrialization, quality, or manufacturing engineering, including at least 5 years in a people leadership role building and scaling a team.
* Demonstrated expertise across DFM/DFA, PPAP, APQP, FMEA, SPC, and structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5 Whys).
* Experience building quality and industrialization systems from the ground up, ideally in a hardware, energy, or battery environment without an established supplier base to lean on.
* Strong technical fluency to go deep with engineers and suppliers, paired with the executive presence to represent risk, tradeoffs, and strategy to senior leadership.
* Comfort operating across the full arc from early design concept through high-volume production and sustaining support, with the judgment to know which problems need a system and which need a phone call.

*#LI-Onsite*

*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*

*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*

*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*

*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.* 
 
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will* ***never*** *solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

Compensation Range: $229,950 - $293,835

existing_roles.description:
"An Equal Opportunity Employer” It is the policy of North American Stamping Group to provide employment, training, promotion, and other conditions of Employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age or status as a qualified individual with a disability or other status protected by law.
 
 
GENERAL SUMMARY
 
Plans, advises, consults, leads, and coordinates manufacturing, manufacturing support, and administration and organizational development activities for one or multiple facilities through Production, Engineering, Maintenance, Purchasing, Quality, Tooling, and Production Control to ensure efficient production of parts with the best material usage, quality levels, and service that exceed the customer’s expectations. Responsible for ensuring all key measures are met from plant and business operations. Leads and promotes matters related to safety, health, environmental, labor control, equipment, material, processes, and customer relations.
 
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
 
A. Serve as management consultant to assigned locations ensuring the management of the company aligns with North American Stamping Group, LLC standard operating procedures and provide subject matter expertise and assistance to increase operating and management efficiency.
 
B. Lead, plan, and manage all manufacturing activities and related functions at assigned locations including production, engineering, maintenance, purchasing, quality, tooling, and production control to ensure safety and quality and to meet and exceed customer and company requirements.
 
1. Lead manufacturing supervision in utilizing Total Quality Production System (TQPS) techniques to standardize processes/methods and to identify manufacturing problems and raw materials/components supply, and eliminate waste.
 
2. Ensure that feasibility studies are carried out correctly for the products to be manufactured at the facility, compatible with the footprint, investment, and quality capabilities planned.
 
3. Develop and monitor Lean activities and a manufacturing continuous improvement system.
 
4. Review launch products and engineering changes implementation and provide direction for successful launch.
 
5. Plan and organize layouts for line changes due to volume changes or manpower reductions.
 
6. Maintain contact with interdepartmental managers to provide feedback when dealing with process or material changes.
 
7. Hold daily staff meetings to communicate daily objectives and discuss successes, failures, and countermeasure activity.
 
8. Ensure NASG philosophies, systems, and processes are being followed at all times.
 
9. Maintain Master Capacity Plan for the facility for accurate budget and capital needs.
 
C. Lead and direct both strategic planning and tactical execution of manufacturing, manufacturing support, and administration functions.
 
D. Understand and execute all plant policies and procedures.
 
1. Structure and implement plant policies and procedures to ensure safe and efficient operation of the company and its associates.
 
2. Ensure alignment of plant policies and procedures, including associate handbook, with corporate policies and procedures.
 
3. Manage plant practices and procedures in compliance with company and industry standards (e.g., IATF16949 and ISO14001).
 
E. Lead development and management of annual plan, budget, key measures, operating efficiency, and cost control.
 
1. Develop annual plan and budget for plant aligned with corporate goals as the foundation to keep the plant moving in a safe, quality conscious, and efficient upward trend.
 
2. Review quotations of new products to ensure compliance with the manufacturing footprint and investment/manpower plans.
 
3. Administer annual plan that incorporates safety, quality, productivity, cost reduction, and associate morale.
 
4. Mutually establish goals and objectives with VP, Manufacturing quarterly.
 
5. Ensure plant goals are met and kept on track.
 
6. Develop, plan, and maintain the budget for plant including making adjustments to achieve targets. Maintain direct and indirect labor budgets while meeting quality and order fill requirements.
 
7. Review and track posted daily, weekly, and monthly goals (including Key Measure targets and results), spot potential problems, and lead in formulating and implementing short-term and long-term countermeasures and solutions.
 
8. Review and plan headcount weekly for labor cost control and operating equipment efficiency (OEE).
 
9. Support and resolve accounts receivable issues with the finance team to ensure timely collection.
 
10. Oversee the monthly reporting documents that are finalized for the plant, ensuring accuracy and completion. Report out monthly reports with targets. Conduct Monthly Management Review meetings.
 
11. Lead management discussions and planning sessions to help formulate cost reduction, waste reduction, product improvement, and problem solving activities, and present operational performance daily/weekly.
 
F. Act as key contact for customers and local industry groups.
 
1. Conduct plant tours and host customer meetings as required.
 
2. Ensure all parts are made to customer requirements in accordance with company policy.
 
3. Support activities to develop and improve customer relations and obtain future business opportunities.
 
4. Develop relationships with local industry groups including those related to manufacturing, automotive, human resources, education and training, legal services, and financial.
 
G. Manage and direct staff in assigned Manufacturing group with a focus on equipment, processes, human resource allocation, cost management, setting priorities, removing roadblocks, and leading through problem identification and resolution, and implementation of short- and long-term corrective actions to manufacturing problems.
 
1. Assign production and engineering staff to support all assigned projects on time and budget with accepted quality.
 
2. Lead staff in activities to meet and improve standard costs of operation both in material and output; minimize downtime; maintain good 5S at all times; reduce cost of quality internal/external failure and PPM; optimize material utilization; optimize raw material, WIP, and finished goods inventory; improve material specifications; and maintain preventative maintenance program.
 
3. Develop and maintain positive associate relations centered on mutual trust, dignity, respect, fairness, consistency, two-way communication, teamwork, and harmony.
 
4. Provide direction and motivation to associates emphasizing quality, efficiency, productivity, cost reduction, safety and health, and morale.
 
5. Ensure further development of associates through performance evaluation, development of training plans, feedback, coaching, and cascade training. Update associate training matrix and schedule any needed training.
 
6. Conduct monthly meetings with associates to communicate state of business.
 
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/REQUIREMENTS
 
 
**Education:** 

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Engineering, or related field preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.
* Auditor training through ISO 14001/IATF16949 preferred.

**Experience:** 

* At least 10 years of functional leadership experience as a manager in a manufacturing environment, preferably automotive stamping.
* Minimum of 12 years of relevant work experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably in automotive stamping, welding, and/or related components (e.g., seating, emissions, ride control, NVH, tooling, and other miscellaneous components).

**Personal/Technical Skills:** 

* General understanding and working knowledge of manufacturing, assembly, and welding equipment and tooling including design, automation, robotics, or manufacturing processes (and all secondary related processes) relating to automotive stamping.
* Working knowledge of tool, gauges and equipment design, automation, robotics, and/or manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience and working knowledge of Basic Equipment Care (BEC) and Preventive Maintenance Optimization (PMO) systems for machinery, tooling, and gauges.
* Practical experience applying Lean principles in an automotive environment.
* General understanding and practical work experience with automotive quality systems and processes.
* Working knowledge of material types specifications and characteristics used in automotive stampings.
* Practical experience applying Total Quality Production System (TQPS) principles in an automotive environment.
* Thorough understanding of company product, trade terminology, quality management and control systems and techniques, manufacturing processes including material controls, work flow, scheduling, kanban, and equipment and machine operation.
* Versed in statistical data entry and utilization of trend analysis.
* Ability to implement plans to control and maintain safety, quality, 5S, cost, and efficiency for assigned areas.

**Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, results-driven **Plant Manager** to lead all daily manufacturing and facility operations. In this role, you will oversee production performance, quality standards, equipment maintenance, and environmental health and safety (EHS/OSHA) compliance. You will manage plant-level budgets, drive improvement initiatives, and build a high-performing, accountable team.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership, coordination, direction and oversight of management/supervisory personnel assigned to power generation facilities.
* Review, analyze, plan, coordinate, and lead all activities within the Operations Department.
* Ensure plant availability and execution of operating and maintenance schedules in conjunction with Plant Staff. • Enforce OSHA, NERC and Environmental permit regulations, investigating accidents, and tracking safety violations.
* Improve processes to optimize asset performance.
* Direct preventive/predictive maintenance programs and coordinate major plant overhauls or planned outages to minimize downtown.
* Establish goals to provide continual improvement in operational productivity and quality.
* Facilitate operational and process engineering changes as necessary.
* Provide oversight to foster an environment that encourages employee involvement.
* Provide guidance and support to ensure safety, environmental, and regulatory compliance.
* Coordinate fulfillment of obligations to its contract counterparties and the energy markets.
* Prepare and manage annual operating and labor budgets, vendor contracts, parts inventory and cost control initiatives.
* Hire, train, schedule and evaluate plant operators, engineers and maintenance staff.
* Ensure compliance with all company standards, practices and policies.
* Oversee the administration of all computerized databases, file systems, and reporting systems for the collection and processing of plant related data.
* Perform other duties as deemed necessary by Owner and VP of Operations.

**Skills**

* A bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline or equivalent experience preferred.
* A minimum of 10-15 years’ experience in hydroelectric, steam and/or electric power plant operations.
* A minimum of 5 years’ management experience.
* Practical knowledge of power generation systems, boilers, gas turbines, and equipment maintenance.
* Mechanical knowledge, electrical systems familiarity, and engineering troubleshooting ability; technical proficiency with plant equipment and P&IDs.
* Understanding of water and wastewater treatment, pipelines, oil and gas operations, safety regulations, and environmental compliance.

existing_roles.title: Director of Contract Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
**Position Summary:**

**The Director of Contract Manufacturing** focuses activities and resources in the organization around value creation and has responsibility for the success of the value stream. Unlike Steffes’ product-line business units, Contract Manufacturing does not own a product line; it markets and sells Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services, building to customer designs, specifications, and requirements.

The Director of Contract Manufacturing understands key system constraints, quickly identifies critical process issues and successfully maintains key customer relationships. Has management responsibility for the strategy, relationship management, pricing and margin.

This role must have excellent business, manufacturing, and technical knowledge; as well as interpersonal skills to communicate and be an influencer, both internal and external to the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Maintains responsibility for assigned business unit, including profitability, business development and budgeting.

* Develops sales and promotional strategies for Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services within the Value Stream.

* Sets vision, defines direction, influences and inspires others, aligns and leads teams to create value and grow the business.

* Responsible for increasing and tracking contract manufacturing revenue and market share.

* Responsible for advancing key customer relationships.

* Works with other department leaders to aid in allocation of resources and capacity to achieve specific business results.

* Coaches and assists team members.

* Sets clear expectations for the customer program life cycle, from quote through production and delivery, and ensures the team understands goals and expectations.

* Identifies risks and establishes suitable actions.

* Responsible for overall customer experience and customer care.

* Maintains a deep understanding of Steffes’ engineering and production processes, capabilities, and capacity.

* Ensures accurate and timely technical reviews of customer designs, drawings, and requirements.

* Establishes pricing based on cost estimates and market value such that market share and profitability goals can be met.

* Maintains a good understanding of competing contract manufacturers and engineering service providers, including their capabilities, marketing strategies, and relative costs. Be capable of effectively communicating this information with the sales department and other functional areas.

* Works with account managers to develop strategies to sell Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services to current and prospective customers.

* Ensures Steffes’ contract manufacturing services are competitive from the standpoint of quality, reliability, cost, lead time, and on-time shipping by calling out deficiencies and seeing proper action is initiated to correct problem areas.

* Monthly maintains financial forecasting and price reviews.

* Communicates with internal staff on a regular basis to understand their business problems and help find solutions.

* Maintains a positive work atmosphere by acting and communicating in a collaborative manner with customers, suppliers, co-workers, and management.

* Helps company meet its Strategic, Quality, and Safety objectives.

* Assists with development and execution of annual sales plans.

* Establishes and maintains guidelines for pursuing and accepting new business.

* Daily monitors shipping activity, costing and pricing to ensure sales and profitability goals are being achieved.

* Assists CFO with review of Terms & Conditions and MSA’s and negotiates with the customer to resolve differences.

* Ensures prompt and satisfactory resolution to external quality issues on customer parts and assemblies.

* Other duties may be assigned

**Job Requirements/Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering or equivalent experience preferred.
* 5 years of experience working in engineering, manufacturing, marketing, or sales
* Experience selling or managing engineering and/or contract manufacturing services with customers.
* Intermediate computer knowledge (Windows, email, internet, etc.)
* Written and verbal communication skills
* Overnight travel is required occasionally

-OR-

* An acceptable combination of education and experience

**Functional & Cognitive Requirements of Position**

* This position requires walking, sitting or standing to a significant degree.
* Must have the ability to lift 50 pounds from floor to waist, carry 50 pounds, and push and/or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Must have the ability to climb ladders and/or stairs.
* Stooping, crouching, kneeling and bending.
* Handling, feeling, and gripping would be required for some activities.
* Visual acuity is required to inspect work completed.
* This role may be subject to internal and external environmental conditions.
* Learn new tasks, remember processes, maintain focus, complete tasks independently, make timely decisions in the context of a workflow, ability to communicate with visitors, ability to complete tasks in situations that have a speed or productivity quota.

**Core Values:** 
**Trust:** We promote growth and long-term success by making wise decisions with trust as an essential component. 
**Respect:** We unleash creative talents of our diverse workforce by treating each other the way we would like to be treated. 
**Teamwork**: We believe people achieve much more by working together. 
**Integrity:** We follow through and keep our word while being open, honest, ethical, and fair. 
**Safety:** We view our co-workers as family members of our business and strive to ensure safety for all. • Humility: We recognize and appreciate strengths and contributions beyond one’s self. We are modest, genuine, and authentic. 
 
**Core Expectations:** 
**Customer Service** - Demonstrate excellent customer service and display a positive attitude and behavior consistent with the Steffes Code of Conduct and Core Values. 
**Environmental, Health, Safety (EHS)** – Perform work in compliance with EHS training and identified procedures/standard work. Report any EHS incident or concern to your supervisor immediately. Cooperate and contribute to the overall success of the EHS program. 
**Quality** – Participate in job-specific training. Complete work as indicated by standard work, processes, and/or procedures. If your work can’t be completed as required, notify your supervisor immediately for guidance. 
**Conduct** - Demonstrate and support the Steffes Code of Conduct. 
**Policies and Procedures** - Demonstrate and support Steffes Policies and Procedures by: 
o Using tact, sound judgement, and maintaining a professional attitude in communication and relationships with others. 
o Striving to deliver the best quality in daily work. 
o Promoting a positive image of Steffes and its products. 
o Being timely and punctual in attendance and following all policies and procedures.

*Equal Opportunity Employer*

existing_roles.title: Plant/Manufacturing Director
existing_roles.description:
Job Summary
 
Maker’s Pride is seeking a proven, enterprise-minded Plant Director to lead our largest manufacturing facility in McComb, Ohio, a site of more than 1,600 Team Members that is critical to the success of our business. The Plant Director holds full accountability for the safety, quality, service, cost, and people performance of a large-scale co-manufacturing operation, and serves as the senior leader on site and the face of the plant to customers, Team Members, and the community.
 
This role requires a seasoned operations executive who has led large, complex plants of 1,000+ Team Members, can build and develop a strong leadership bench, and can balance day-to-day execution with long-term strategy. The Plant Director partners closely with senior leadership and corporate functions to deliver the plant’s operating plan, drive operational excellence, and position McComb for sustained growth.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Operational Leadership: Lead all plant operations, including production, packaging, maintenance, engineering, quality, warehouse, and supply chain, to consistently deliver safety, quality, service, and cost targets across multiple shifts and lines.
* P&L and Financial Accountability: Own the plant’s operating plan, budget, and financial performance, including labor, overtime, yield, waste, and capital spend. Identify and execute cost-reduction and margin-improvement opportunities.
* Strategic Planning: Develop and execute a multi-year plant strategy aligned to enterprise goals, covering capacity, capital investment, automation, new business onboarding, and talent.
* Production Planning and Capacity: Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, and Customer teams to build production schedules and resource plans that optimize throughput, labor utilization, and on-time, in-full performance.
* Quality and Food Safety: Ensure strict adherence to quality, food safety, and regulatory requirements (e.g., FDA, GMP, HACCP, and customer and third-party audit standards). Drive corrective and preventive actions and maintain audit readiness at all times.
* Safety Culture: Champion a zero-harm culture. Enforce safety policies, lead regular audits and incident reviews, and hold the leadership team accountable for proactive hazard prevention and compliance.
* Workforce Strategy and Labor Relations: Partner with HR to attract, retain, and engage a large and diverse workforce. Drive staffing stability, reduce turnover, manage overtime effectively, and foster positive Team Member and labor relations, including compliance with applicable employment and labor laws and agreements.
* Customer and Partner Relationships: Serve as the senior site representative with co-manufacturing customers, hosting visits and audits, resolving escalations, and building long-term trust. Collaborate with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of materials and finished goods.
* Continuous Improvement: Lead a data-driven operational excellence program using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies to eliminate waste, improve OEE and yield, and standardize best practices across shifts.
* Capital and Asset Management: Oversee capital planning, project execution, and asset reliability to ensure equipment, infrastructure, and facilities support safe, efficient, and scalable operations.
* Reporting and Executive Communication: Provide regular, transparent reporting on safety, quality, production, financial, and workforce KPIs to senior leadership, with clear analysis, risks, and recommendations.
* Community and Site Presence: Represent Maker’s Pride in the McComb community and maintain a visible, accessible leadership presence on the plant floor across all shifts.

Supervisory Responsibilities
 

* Leadership of a Large Organization: Provide direct leadership to the plant leadership team and overall leadership of 1,600+ Team Members, including managers, supervisors, technicians, and support staff.
* Talent Development: Build a strong leadership bench through coaching, performance management, succession planning, and development of high-potential leaders.
* Culture and Accountability: Foster a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, respect, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications
 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
* Experience: 15+ years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including 7+ years in a senior plant leadership role (Plant Manager, Plant Director, or equivalent).
* Scale: Demonstrated success leading large, complex, multi-shift plants of 1,000+ Team Members, with full P&L accountability.
* Industry: Experience in co-manufacturing, food, beverage, or other high-volume, regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
* Operational Excellence: Track record of delivering measurable improvements in safety, quality, productivity, and cost. Lean, Six Sigma, or similar certification desirable.
* Workforce Leadership: Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop a large, diverse workforce, including strong experience with staffing, retention, and employee and labor relations. Experience in a unionized environment is a plus.
* Regulatory Knowledge: Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, food safety and quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Technology: Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office Suite; experience with manufacturing software (e.g., SAP, Oracle) is a plus.
* Leadership Skills: Strategic thinker with excellent executive presence, communication, and decision-making skills; able to influence at all levels of the organization and with customers.
* Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with a focus on data-driven decision-making.

The information provided in this document provides an overview of the most common duties, qualifications, and demands of the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive summary of the role, and the duties, qualifications, and demands of the position are subject to change without notice. The expectations provided here may also be modified if an employee with a disability could effectively meet the expectations for the role with reasonable accommodation.

existing_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $155,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY** 
The Environmental Health and Safety Director leads the development, implementation, and performance of health, safety, and environmental programs and policies at Lassonde Pappas & Co. Inc. facilities, to maintain compliance with applicable national and local regulations and to ensure a safe, healthy working environment for all employees. This role reports to the VP of Manufacturing for the US and is based out of our Cherry Hill, New Jersey location.

**Primary Responsibilities include*****:***

* Oversee and ensure the organization’s compliance with local, state, and federal environment, health, and safety regulations including (but not limited to) fire safety and OSHA regulations, and keep up with any changes to laws and regulations that impact the organization
* Work closely with the organization’s legal department to ensure that the company is in compliance with these regulations
* Direct audits and work with each plant and its departments to ensure that all company guidelines are being followed
* Manage the safety budget at the manufacturing sites to ensure that appropriate personal protective and safety equipment is available as needed to prevent injuries and provide for a safe and healthy work environment
* Develop, implement, and evaluate programs, policies, and procedures related to health, safety, and environmental issues in the workplace, and ensure that environmental policy and procedure manuals are available and updated at all times to reduce the risk of injury or illness in the workplace
* Prepare, schedule, and execute training to cover emergency procedures, workplace safety, and other relevant topics
* Lead the planning, execution, monitoring and continuous improvement of environmental health and safety programs
* Conduct risk assessments of work sites to identify potential hazards and formulate plans to mitigate them
* Coordinate with insurance carriers to ensure that appropriate coverage is in place to cover any potential risks
* Review the employee accident reports and medical claims to evaluate the need for potential changes to current policies or procedures
* Consult with engineers to ensure that building designs are safe and compliant with current regulations
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Maintain staff by training employees; maintaining a safe, secure, and legal work environment; developing personal growth opportunities.
* Set objectives, monitor performance, and develop individual training plans to support professional development

* Communicate job expectations; planning, monitoring, and assessing job results; coaching, and counseling employees; developing, coordinating, and enforcing systems, procedures, and productivity standards.
* Establish strategic goals; identifying and evaluating trends; choosing a course of action; defining objectives; evaluating outcomes.
* Set strategic direction and coordinate the work of others to achieve objectives.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Safety, Occupational Safety and Health, or related field required; Masters degree desirable.

* Minimum 8 years working experience in Supply Chain environment in Food and Beverage or other perishable goods
* 5+ years of safety and environmental experience in a manufacturing environment. Experience with a union manufacturing environment is a plus.
* Excellent negotiation skills and the ability to influence others while maintaining professionalism
* Proficient in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook (knowledge in Excel should extend past spreadsheet manipulation and should include creation of formulas)
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed oriented and can multi-task
* Excellent time management skills

**Additional Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food/beverage industry
* Experience in Manufacturing or production environment
* Experience with risk management and project management
* Must pay high attention to detail and have strong interpersonal, communication, and observation skills
* Experience in report writing
* Proven organizational skills
* Ability to direct, coach, and train others
* Consultative, influential, strategic thinking and problem-solving skills

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle and occasionally working in the field/production setting.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

**OCCASIONAL:** squatting, kneeling, reach above and at shoulder height, moderate grasp to manipulate reference books and manuals; lifting objects weighing 20 – 35 lbs. from below waist to above shoulders and transporting distances up to 50 feet.

**Department:** Operations **Job Status:** Full Time

**FLSA Status:** Exempt **Reports To:** President

**Job Type:** Non-Union **Amount of Travel Required:** Occasional

**Work Schedule:** Monday – Friday

Evenings, weekends, Holidays as needed. **Positions Supervised:** Production Staff

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Essential Functions Statement(s)**

 

* Improve operational efficiencies to reduce total production costs while meeting specific product volume needs
* Check and verify production records, handle questions or concerns of inventory shortages or overages and address problems with inventory control.
* Coordinate production schedules to meet sales demand. Adjust production as necessary to meet seasonal demands ahead of schedule.
* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.

existing_roles.title: Director of Program Management, Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

KRUSH Tech is an international technology company developing advanced hardware solutions for defense, aerospace, communications, and autonomous systems. We're launching our U.S. operations from the ground up, building a next-generation, vertically integrated aerospace organization focused on advanced uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), autonomy, and sensing technologies for the U.S. market and strategic partners. Our teams work across RF, embedded systems, electronics, mechanical engineering, software, manufacturing, and supply chain to turn some of the industry's most demanding engineering challenges into reliable, production-ready solutions, combining the agility of a startup with the ambition to compete at the leading edge of UAS and autonomous systems.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Director of Program Management to lead program delivery for KRUSH's uncrewed aircraft systems, from development through production and fielding. This senior leadership role owns cost, schedule, and technical delivery performance across a portfolio of cross-functional programs, aligns engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and test around clear milestones, and serves as the point of accountability for customers and partners.

Reporting to the Vice President of Manufacturing Operations, you will build program management discipline in a start-up U.S. operation: light enough to move fast, and rigorous enough to meet customer commitments. You will partner closely with engineering and manufacturing leaders to take products from concept through production ramp, balancing competing priorities, risks, and resources across programs.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

* Own cost, schedule, scope, and technical delivery performance across a portfolio of programs, from development through production and fielding
* Develop and implement program management strategy, governance, and standards, using lightweight processes and tools that fit a fast-moving start-up
* Ensure programs align with corporate objectives and strategic priorities, and lead portfolio reviews that prioritize initiatives by business value and strategic impact
* Build, lead, and develop the program management team as the organization grows, including career development and succession planning
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, and Test leaders to drive decisions, manage dependencies, and resolve issues across functions
* Lead the transition of programs from development into production, including readiness reviews and stage-gate decisions
* Manage portfolio resource allocation, monitor program performance and interdependencies, and balance competing priorities
* Serve as the primary interface with customers, executive leadership, and external partners, communicating program status, risks, opportunities, and outcomes, and facilitating steering committees and executive reviews
* Develop and manage program budgets and forecasts, monitor financial performance, evaluate business cases and return on investment, and support annual planning and investment prioritization
* Identify, assess, and mitigate program risks and issues, and develop contingency plans for critical risks
* Lead change management and organizational readiness activities for program changes
* Ensure compliance with governance, regulatory, export control, and contractual requirements
* Implement program and portfolio management tools and reporting systems, and define and track program KPIs, including on-time milestone achievement, budget adherence, resource utilization, and risk mitigation effectiveness
* Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, and delivery excellence

 **Requirements**

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field
* 10+ years of program and project management experience, preferably in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability hardware
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing large programs or a PMO function
* Experience leading cross-functional, hardware-intensive programs from development through production
* Experience managing programs under customer or government contracts, including cost, schedule, and deliverable performance
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional strategic initiatives and to influence executive stakeholders
* Strong skills in program and portfolio management, strategic planning, financial and budget management, risk and issue management, change management, and resource planning
* Strong data analysis and executive reporting skills, with experience in business process improvement
* Strong leadership, negotiation, and influencing skills
* Active U.S. Secret security clearance, with the ability to maintain it
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 50% of the time
* Must qualify as a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities (ITAR)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Master's degree (MBA or equivalent)
* Familiarity with defense contracting and acquisition processes, including FAR/DFARS, contract types, CDRLs, and earned value management
* Experience building a program management function or PMO at a start-up or high-growth company
* PMP or an equivalent program management certification

 **Benefits**

KRUSH Tech offers a competitive compensation package. Compensation is determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual offers are determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on interview performance, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, and internal equity.

The salary range provided is a good faith estimate of the applicable range as of the date of posting. The final offer will be determined after considering all relevant factors, including a candidate's qualifications and experience.

In addition to base pay, KRUSH Tech offers a monthly benefits stipend that employees can apply toward the health, dental, vision, or other coverage that best fits their needs, along with 9 paid federal holidays per year.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

KRUSH Tech is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

**Reasonable Accommodation Statement**

KRUSH Tech is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and hiring process and during employment. If you require assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact Human Resources.

Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route. 
 
Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director is responsible for leading and coordinating key operational functions of the manufacturing facility, including **Production Planning, Supply Chain, Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), and Infrastructure/Construction Engineering**.

This position plays a critical role in ensuring production readiness, material availability, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, facility development, and cross-functional execution.

The Operations Director will work closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Finance, Human Resources, and other functional leaders to support safe, efficient, and scalable operations of the Chicago manufacturing facility.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Production Planning & Operations Coordination**

* Lead production planning and scheduling based on demand, capacity, materials, and priorities.
* Develop and manage short- and long-term production plans.
* Coordinate manpower, equipment, and materials to achieve production targets.
* Monitor plan execution and identify delivery risks.
* Drive cross-functional efforts to resolve production and operational constraints.
* Track key KPIs, including production attainment, inventory, material availability, delivery, and efficiency.
* Support S&OP and capacity planning processes.

* **Supply Chain Management**

* Lead plant supply chain operations, including production planning, materials, procurement, inventory, warehousing, and logistics.
* Ensure material availability while maintaining optimal inventory levels.

* Establish and manage operational processes across planning, supply chain, EHS, and infrastructure.
* Lead operational reviews and drive action item completion.

* **Team Leadership**

* Lead, develop, and mentor managers and operational teams.
* Establish organizational structure, goals, and succession plans.
* Recruit, develop, and retain key talent.

* Foster a collaborative, safety-focused, high-performance culture.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field required.
* Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* **10+ years of progressive experience** in manufacturing operations, supply chain, production planning, engineering, or related functions.
* **5+ years of leadership experience** managing managers and/or multiple operational functions.
* Strong experience in large-scale manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience in production planning, supply chain management, and plant operations.
* Working knowledge of EHS management and U.S. regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting facility construction, plant expansion, infrastructure, or manufacturing engineering projects strongly preferred.
* Strong knowledge of ERP/MRP systems; SAP experience preferred.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in **lithium-ion battery, EV, automotive, energy storage, electronics, or advanced manufacturing**.
* Experience supporting the launch or ramp-up of a new manufacturing facility in the United States.
* Experience managing complex global supply chains.
* Familiarity with high-volume automated manufacturing environments.
* Experience working with international and cross-cultural teams.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, S&OP, inventory optimization, and operational excellence methodologies.
* PMP, APICS/CPIM/CSCP, Six Sigma, or related professional certification is a plus.

The Operations Director provides leadership and management oversight for:

**Infrastructure / Construction / Facility Engineering**

existing_roles.description:
Position Overview

We are partnering with an established, innovative manufacturer of advanced semiconductor capital equipment to identify an experienced Director of Manufacturing Operations.

This highly visible leadership position is responsible for overseeing a complex manufacturing organization, driving operational excellence, and ensuring the successful assembly, integration, testing, and delivery of sophisticated capital equipment systems.

The ideal candidate is a decisive, hands-on operations leader who thrives in a fast-paced, technically complex manufacturing environment. This individual will bring a strong sense of ownership and accountability, with the ability to develop high-performing teams, solve challenging operational problems, and consistently deliver against customer commitments.

This role requires a strategic thinker who is equally comfortable managing day-to-day factory execution, driving continuous improvement initiatives, and communicating manufacturing performance, financial results, and operational strategy to executive leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Operations & Execution

* Lead daily manufacturing operations across sub-assembly, system assembly, integration, and final test functions.
* Take direct ownership of manufacturing performance, including on-time shipments, product quality, production schedules, and customer commitments.
* Establish and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with organizational objectives, customer requirements, and business growth.
* Identify and resolve production bottlenecks, resource constraints, and operational challenges to maintain consistent factory output.
* Drive operational accountability through clearly defined performance metrics, structured problem-solving, and decisive leadership.
* Ensure manufacturing capacity, staffing, and production resources are aligned with business demand.

Financial & Operational Management

* Develop and manage manufacturing operating budgets, resource plans, labor utilization, and production costs.
* Monitor and communicate key financial and operational metrics, including manufacturing output, revenue-related shipment performance, labor overhead, operating expenses, and production capacity.
* Present manufacturing performance, operational risks, and improvement initiatives to senior executive leadership.
* Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency, resource utilization, and overall manufacturing productivity.
* Support strategic business planning through accurate capacity assessments, operational forecasting, and data-driven decision-making.

Leadership & Organizational Development

* Lead, mentor, and develop a manufacturing organization consisting of production managers, supervisors, engineers, technicians, and operational support personnel.
* Establish a culture of accountability, ownership, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Evaluate organizational capabilities, identify leadership gaps, and implement development plans to strengthen management effectiveness.
* Make timely, well-informed decisions to address performance issues, operational challenges, and organizational needs.
* Build a high-performance manufacturing culture focused on execution, safety, quality, and customer satisfaction.
* Promote effective cross-functional collaboration with engineering, quality, supply chain, and executive leadership.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

* Champion a proactive safety culture and ensure compliance with applicable manufacturing safety and quality standards.
* Drive improvements in product quality, first-pass yield, manufacturing consistency, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead structured root-cause investigations and corrective action initiatives using methodologies such as 8D, Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and statistical process control.
* Develop and execute continuous improvement roadmaps focused on cycle-time reduction, process efficiency, waste elimination, and operational scalability.
* Implement proactive quality initiatives that identify and resolve manufacturing issues earlier in the production process.
* Maintain compliance with applicable ISO certifications and established quality management systems.

Manufacturing Engineering & Process Optimization

* Partner with engineering and manufacturing teams to improve product manufacturability, assembly efficiency, and test effectiveness.
* Drive improvements in manufacturing test strategies, including modular testing, parallel test execution, and automated test methods.
* Identify opportunities to reduce final system test cycle times while maintaining rigorous product quality standards.
* Support new product introductions, engineering changes, and production transitions to ensure manufacturing readiness.
* Collaborate with global suppliers and contract manufacturing partners to support production requirements and operational objectives.
* Lead manufacturing-related insourcing, outsourcing, and production transfer initiatives as required.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Operations Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing or operations, including at least 5 years in a manufacturing operations leadership role within the semiconductor capital equipment industry.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex capital equipment manufacturing operations, including assembly, integration, testing, and final product delivery.
* Proven accountability for factory performance, production output, on-time shipments, manufacturing quality, and operational execution.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor costs, overhead, capacity planning, and production-related financial performance.
* Ability to communicate operational results, financial performance, manufacturing risks, and strategic recommendations effectively to executive leadership.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing teams and developing managers in a demanding, high-performance environment.
* Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, structured problem-solving, quality management systems, and data-driven operational improvement.
* Decisive leadership style with a demonstrated ability to solve problems, make difficult decisions, and drive accountability across an organization.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience manufacturing sophisticated semiconductor processing or precision capital equipment systems.
* Experience leading manufacturing organizations of approximately 100 employees, including multiple direct-report managers.
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Value Stream Mapping, and continuous improvement programs.
* Experience with SAP, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and advanced manufacturing analytics tools.
* Proven success reducing manufacturing cycle times, improving production throughput, and implementing automated or modular final test strategies.
* Experience applying Design for Manufacturability (DfM) principles in collaboration with engineering and product development teams.
* Experience supporting international supply chains, global supplier relationships, and contract manufacturing operations.
* Familiarity with new product introduction, manufacturing transfer, and production scalability initiatives.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will be a confident, results-oriented manufacturing leader who combines strong technical manufacturing knowledge with exceptional operational discipline and business judgment.

This individual should have a proven track record of leading complex semiconductor capital equipment (low-volume/high-mix) manufacturing organizations, improving factory performance, and developing accountable, high-performing teams.

They must be comfortable operating at both the strategic and tactical levels—whether presenting operational and financial performance to executive leadership, making critical production decisions, resolving manufacturing challenges, or coaching managers to improve execution.

Above all, this role requires a leader who takes ownership, drives decisions, holds teams accountable, and consistently delivers measurable operational results.

Additional Information

* Onsite leadership position based in San Jose, California.
* Occasional domestic and international travel may be required.
* Opportunity to lead a technically sophisticated manufacturing organization with significant visibility and influence across the business.
