existing_roles.title: Director of Planning and Production Coordination
existing_roles.description:
**POSITION:** Director of Planning and Production Coordination

**SHIFT:** Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm + Additional hours based on business demand

**SALARY:** $139,362 - $155,161.50 + (DOE) + Full Benefits Package

**LOCATION: On-site in office in Fargo, ND**

### **SUMMARY OF RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Director of Planning and Production Coordination leads enterprise planning and production coordination across CSP, Tank and Structural product lines. The role establishes consistent planning standards, aligns demand with capacity, ensures production readiness, balances workloads across sites and supports reliable customer commitments. The role owns the planning system and coordination processes.

### **ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS**

* Embrace and demonstrate the qualities of the TrueNorth Steel Game Changer definition.
* Comply with all safety, quality, environmental and workplace requirements.
* Lead, coach, and develop the CSP, Tank and Structural Planning Leaders and the Production Coordinator Supervisor, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and succession coverage.
* Establish and continuously improve an integrated planning and production-coordination system with common standards, planning horizons, terminology, decision rights, data requirements, and escalation paths.
* Align customer demand, forecasts, backlog, inventory, labor, equipment, material availability, and site capability into executable production plans.
* Confirm customer commit-date feasibility using verified readiness, material, capacity, outside-processing, site, and delivery information.
* Provide an enterprise view of capacity and constraints, leading approved workload-balancing actions such as site transfers, priority changes, outsourcing, overtime, and staffing adjustments.
* Define and enforce production-readiness requirements for drawings, bills of material, routing, material, CNC and nesting information, quality requirements, outside services, job packets, shipping information, and approvals.
* Lead regular site, product-line, and enterprise planning reviews that surface demand, capacity, backlog, readiness, schedule performance, risks, and decisions requiring action.
* Partner with Manufacturing, Sales, Project Management, Estimating, Drafting, Engineering, Purchasing, Inventory Control, Quality, Shipping, Logistics, Finance, and other functions to resolve planning constraints.
* Govern planning and production coordination data and transactions in SyteLine, Tekla and other approved systems, including capacity assumptions, work-center data, production status, and readiness information.
* Define performance measures and dashboards for schedule, backlog, capacity, readiness, equipment use, changes, and failure-related costs. Use data to improve delivery, throughput, material utilization, and profitability.
* Establish repeatable standard work, documentation, training, cross-training, and backup coverage to reduce dependence on individual knowledge.
* Serve as the escalation point for significant cross-site, cross-product, and cross-functional planning issues. Elevate unresolved matters with facts, alternatives, risks, and recommendations.
* Support annual business, capacity, capital, workforce, and budget planning, along with strategic manufacturing initiatives.
* Provide the VP of Manufacturing with regular updates on planning risks, delivery, capacity, material, organizational needs, trends, and recommended actions.
* Travel to manufacturing sites is required to understand processes, build relationships, support teams, and ensure consistent implementation of planning and production-coordination standards.
* Prompt and dependable attendance.
* Other duties as assigned.

### **KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND QUALITIES**

* Strong knowledge of manufacturing planning, scheduling, capacity management, production coordination, inventory, and shop-floor execution.
* Ability to lead leaders and standardize planning processes across multiple manufacturing sites or business units.
* Working knowledge of ERP-supported planning, bills of material, routing, work centers, job release, inventory, and production transactions.
* Strong analytical judgment and ability to balance customer commitments, manufacturing capability, cost, and business risk.
* Effective communication, facilitation, change leadership and cross-functional influence skills.
* High integrity, accountability, attention to detail, sound judgment, and bias toward action.
* Commitment to safety, quality, customer service, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

### **EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, Construction Management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
* Minimum of ten years of progressive responsible experience in manufacturing operations, planning, scheduling, supply chain, project coordination, or a related field preferred, including five years of leadership experience.
* Experience leading multi-site planning or operational processes, ERP-supported planning and cross-functional improvement preferred.
* Experience in steel fabrication, metal manufacturing, project-based manufacturing, or a related industrial environment preferred.

existing_roles.description:
**About Mayzo, Inc.**

Since 1986, Mayzo has been a trusted global supplier of specialty chemical additives and innovative material solutions that help manufacturers create safer, more efficient, and more sustainable products. Our technologies support a wide range of industries by improving product performance, enhancing manufacturing processes, reducing waste, and lowering costs.

As a privately held company, Mayzo combines the agility and entrepreneurial spirit of a growing organization with the stability, reputation, and financial strength built over nearly four decades. Our success is driven by knowledgeable, passionate employees who are committed to solving complex customer challenges through technical expertise, innovation, and exceptional service.

At Mayzo, we believe our people are our greatest advantage. We foster a collaborative, customer-focused culture where employees are empowered to make an impact, develop professionally, and contribute to meaningful work that supports customers around the world. If you're looking to build your career with a company that values innovation, teamwork, and long-term success, we'd love to hear from you.

**About the Role**

**Department**

Operations

**Reports to**

Vice President of Global Operations

**Type**

Full-Time

**Location**

Mayzo Operations Center in Walterboro, SC

**Overview**

Mayzo is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead the overall performance and continuous improvement of our manufacturing facility in Walterboro, South Carolina. This hands-on leadership role oversees production, safety, quality, maintenance, inventory, shipping and receiving, and employee development. The Plant Manager will ensure products are manufactured safely, efficiently, and in accordance with company standards, customer requirements, and regulatory guidelines while fostering accountability, teamwork, and operational excellence.

This is an opportunity to join a vibrant, privately held company that combines the energy and growth of an entrepreneurial organization with the stability, brand recognition, and solid financial foundation of an established business.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations to achieve production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery expectations.
* Monitor production schedules and coordinate labor, equipment, and other resources to optimize workflow and efficiency.
* Build a strong safety culture and maintain compliance with OSHA requirements, environmental regulations, company policies, and safe work practices.
* Lead investigations involving safety incidents, quality concerns, equipment failures, and operational issues, including corrective and preventive actions.
* Ensure compliance with applicable ISO standards, quality management systems, and customer specifications.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, quality, cost reduction, production yield, and operational efficiency.
* Analyze plant performance metrics, including safety, quality, productivity, labor, inventory, equipment utilization, and financial results.
* Develop, coach, and lead supervisors and plant employees through clear expectations, regular feedback, and professional development.
* Oversee preventive maintenance programs and ensure equipment and facilities support safe, reliable, and efficient operations.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Customer Service, Sales, and Procurement to support inventory availability and on-time customer shipments.
* Develop and manage the plant operating budget and identify cost-saving opportunities without compromising safety or quality.
* Support new product introductions, process improvements, capital projects, and other business objectives.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, or another technical discipline required; industrial engineering or logistics is preferred.
* Minimum of 15 years of business and team management experience in the chemicals industry or a related field; small- or mid-sized company experience is preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in supply chain management, operations management, and/or product management.
* Experience with ERP systems, inventory control, warehousing, logistics, and procurement.
* Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing safety, regulatory compliance, quality systems, budgeting, maintenance, and continuous improvement.
* Proven ability to lead teams, solve complex operational problems, manage projects, and adapt to changing priorities.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises employees within the Mayzo Operations Center.
* Recruits, hires, trains, coaches, and evaluates employees; plans and assigns work; recognizes performance; addresses concerns; and takes corrective action when appropriate.
* Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with Mayzo policies and applicable laws.

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

* Continual standing and walking, with frequent climbing, balancing, bending, stooping, kneeling, or crawling.
* Ability to lift, push, or carry items up to 25 kg (approximately 55 lb.) without assistance.
* Frequent work around fumes, airborne particles, toxic chemicals, production machinery, and loud noise with required PPE.
* Use of specialized equipment or vehicles, including forklifts and scissor lifts.

**Benefits**

* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k)
* Flexible Spending Account and Health Savings Account
* Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* Paid time off

**Core Competencies**

Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company.

We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors and society.

More information is available at www.nrg.com. Connect with NRG on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X.

**Job Summary**
---------------

Responsible for all aspects of Plant Operation and Maintenance, including P&L responsibility. Responsible for maintaining a competent, well-trained staff. Responsible for plant safety, training, environmental compliance, policy administration and has purchasing authority for required materials and services. Maintain good relationship with customers and the community. Responsible for supporting and executing Gas Plant Strategy in a dynamic financial climate. The Aurora and Rockford Generating simple cycle peaking plants are located outside of Chicago. Aurora Generation is a 1000 MW facility operating four GE 7FAs and six GE LM 6000 natural gas-fired combustion turbines. Rockford Generation is a 540MW facility operating three Siemens V84.3A2 natural gas-fired combustion turbines. The two sites are about 70 miles apart.

**Responsibilities:**
---------------------

* Supports and emphasizes importance of safety and environmental programs and ensures regulatory compliance
* Promotes productivity and teamwork with open communication, timely decision making, and use of leadership skills to set high standards of performance, while providing the direction necessary to achieve performance
* Promotes and supports the development of technical leadership and business skills of employees to carry out responsibilities in a competitive environment
* Responsible for matrix communications to NRG management
* Provides regular feedback to employees on their performance to allow them to capitalize on their strengths and focus on opportunities for improvement
* Creates and supports an organizational culture that encourages and rewards employee involvement, innovative thinking, adaptation to change, responsible risk taking, customer focus, and continuous improvement
* Formulates appropriate strategies which support the overall NRG strategy and manages development, implementation and execution of assigned area goals, objectives, and initiatives
* Manages all business aspects of assigned area to maximize competitive position of the plant including operational performance, staff development and cost management
* Reviews organizational performance with constituents and addresses opportunities for improvement on a regular basis
* Manages, as necessary, the evaluation and selection of external service providers.
* Manages work performed by external service providers in support of organizational objectives and responsibilities
* Assigns work and holds employees accountable for their performance
* Develops and maintains professional relationships with organizations external to the plant
* Ensures that appropriate technical expertise related to assigned area of responsibility is available and provided to employees in a timely manner.
* Manages development and execution of appropriate standards, guidelines, programs, and procedures within assigned area of responsibility
* Uses and maintains technical and professional knowledge, shares that knowledge with others, and recognizes/applies new technology in a cost-effective manner
* Obtains and applies knowledge of competitive business practices in daily work activities and decision making
* Seeks and understands the organizational needs and focuses on meeting and exceeding these requirements
* Anticipates, accepts and successfully implements necessary changes in the organization and adapts to meet the new requirements
* Ensure a safe and environmentally compliant workplace
* Willing to accept accountability for own decisions, performance, and behavior, as well as the performance of assigned staff
* Must be able to effectively interface with regulatory, political, business, civic and public representatives consistent with NRG corporate objectives

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

* Minimum of Bachelors degree in an Engineering or related technical discipline, and 10 years of equivalent experience in a related technical field; or a minimum of 14 years experience in a related technical field or similar position
* Demonstrated record of successfully leading/supervising employees in a related field
* Ability to split time between both sites

**Preferred:**

* Experience with GE 7FA, LM6000 and/or Siemens V84.3A2 preferred.
* Experience with remote operations a plus. Aurora responsible for the remote operation of 8 LM6000s in Texas at 4 different sites.

**Competencies:**
-----------------

* Uses and maintains technical and professional knowledge, shares that knowledge with others, and recognizes/applies new technology in a cost effective manner
* Obtains and applies knowledge of competitive business practices in daily work activities and decision making
* Seeks and understands the customer/client’s needs and focuses on meeting and exceeding their expectations
* Anticipates and accepts changes in the organization and adapts to meet the new requirements
* Committed to making the workplace safe and environmentally sound
* Willing to accept accountability for own decisions, performance, and behavior, as well as the performance of assigned employees.

**Working Conditions:**
-----------------------

* Power plant environment.
* Requires operation of a motor vehicle; active Driver’s License.
* Work overtime and non-standard working hours as required
* Requires occasional travel outside service area
* Requires wearing personal protective safety equipment (respirators, safety glasses, hard hat, appropriate footwear, ear plugs, etc.)
* Required to work around rotating and energized equipment, hazardous materials and chemicals
* Requires standing, sitting, walking, kneeling, twisting, climbing stairs and ladders, and entering plant equipment.
* Requires operation of a personal computer
* Occasionally requires lifting as appropriate to perform duties and responsibilities

Actual salaries will vary based on several factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. * We are conducting a confidential search for a Plant Manager with a well-established industrial manufacturer in the Tulsa area.

**What You Will Lead:**

* Safety first, always. Establish and maintain a proactive safety culture through field presence, training, hazard recognition, and accountability.
* Lead daily plant production, scheduling, staffing, equipment readiness, output, and on-time fulfillment.

* Oversee concrete manufacturing processes such as batching, reinforcement, forming and molds, casting, curing, handling, and finished-product inspection.
* Coach supervisors, leads, and hourly employees; develop talent and improve workforce performance, engagement, and accountability.
* Partner with maintenance, engineering, and logistics to reduce downtime, rework, waste, and process bottlenecks.

**What We Are Looking For:**

* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations with direct accountability for workplace safety, quality, production, and labor.
* Strong practical experience in concrete manufacturing is highly preferred; reinforced concrete pipe, culverts, drainage structures, manholes, inlets, vaults, or related products are especially relevant.
* Knowledge of production processes, quality inspections, equipment, maintenance coordination, and continuous improvement.
* Proven ability to lead frontline teams, strengthen supervisors, and solve operational problems on the plant floor.
* Clear communication, sound judgment, and the ability to balance production goals with uncompromising safety standards.
* Bilingual English and Spanish skills are a significant plus, but not a requirement.

**Compensation and Location:**

**What you’ll do:**
-------------------

**Lead one of Eaton’s key B-Line manufacturing operations and help position it for its next stage of growth.**

Eaton’s Global Energy Infrastructure Solutions (GEIS) division is seeking a Plant Manager to lead its **approximately 400-person, non-union manufacturing facility in Sherman, Texas**. This role offers significant leadership scope, combining ownership of plant performance and financial results with the opportunity to **develop the organization, strengthen operational capability, and influence the future direction of the site.**

Reporting to the Director of Operations, you will lead the plant’s strategy and execution while developing a strong leadership team and advancing performance across **safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and employee engagement**. For a manufacturing leader who enjoys both driving results today and building an operation for the future, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact at the site and across the broader business.

GEIS operates within Eaton’s global Electrical Sector, supporting customers in markets being reshaped by **electrification, energy transition, digitalization, and increasing demands for safe and reliable power infrastructure**. With more than a century of industry experience, the business is focused on accelerating growth through innovation, operational excellence, and continued investment in its global manufacturing capabilities.

**What you will need:**
-----------------------

**Essential Functions:**

* Translate business goals into a clear plant strategy, annual operating plan, and measurable priorities, with accountability for achieving the annual budget, managing costs, and delivering sustained operational and financial performance.
* Champion a proactive environmental, health, and safety culture by engaging employees in hazard identification and prevention, ensuring regulatory compliance, and reinforcing personal accountability and Eaton’s standards for ethical conduct.
* Strengthen customer satisfaction by improving product quality, on-time delivery, and productivity, aligning plant execution with customer requirements, and resolving issues that affect service and responsiveness.
* Apply the Eaton Business System and Lean/Six Sigma methods to eliminate waste, address root causes, reduce costs, and improve process reliability through disciplined problem-solving and sustained, measurable improvements.
* Build organizational capability by attracting, developing, coaching, and retaining talent, setting clear expectations, and strengthening leadership capability, employee engagement, and accountability throughout the plant.
* Align manufacturing engineering, safety, quality, supply chain, continuous improvement, HR, and finance around shared priorities, using clear communication and cross-functional collaboration to remove barriers and execute plant objectives.

**Requirements & Additional Information:**
------------------------------------------

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university
* Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing, supply chain, finance, operational excellence, or related manufacturing support functions.

**Additional Information**

* The position will be based onsite at our Sherman, TX manufacturing plant.
* This position will offer relocation within the US.
* Legally authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship. Eaton will not consider applicants for employment, immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.
* Up to 10% travel is required.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $165000 - $242000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

**Role Description:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the management, planning, and coordination of all precast manufacturing operations to meet DVP business goals, while providing leadership to all plant and yard personnel.

**General Supervisory Responsibilities and Duties:**

* Create and manage production schedules based on manpower, customer demand, and DVP business goals
* Meet with General Manager as needed to review any safety concerns, production & quality issues, personnel needs, and inventory levels
* Conducts daily supervisor meetings to discuss production schedules, concerns, opportunities for improvement and to ensure ongoing organizational teamwork
* Hold monthly plant safety meetings and review any safety related deficiencies and submit recommendations to DVP senior management
* Track key performance metrics and hold direct reports accountable for results
* Ensure all production and yard operations meet DVP quality control standards
* Track and manage the inventory levels of finished goods
* Oversee and manage all incoming materials to ensure adequate inventory levels are met
* Continually collect and review data to reduce inefficiencies and waste
* Successfully hire, supervise, train, and retain production/yard staff
* Evaluate and review employee’s performance for the purpose of determining skill level and training needs
* Coach and mentor employees to allow for increased responsibilities and career advancement. Lead by example.
* Promote and maintain a clean work environment
* Recommend purchases of additional equipment for efficiency, cost reductions and/or quality improvements
* Successfully work with Quality Control/Project Management to meet customer demand and expectations
* Perform any other duties as assigned by the General Manager

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Supervision of Plant Supervisors
* Leading by example, create and sustain a safe working environment for the facility

**Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Eligible to work in the U.S
* Successful experience in precast plant management
* Ability to read contract documents, engineering specifications and drawings
* Strong interpersonal and leadership skills
* Excellent time management skills
* Highly organized and self-motivated
* Strong oral and written communication skills
* Work with computer as necessary (Microsoft Word, Excel)

**Physical Requirements:**

* Standing and walking for extended periods of time
* Exposure to fluctuating weather conditions including extreme cold or heat
* Must be in good physical and mental health

**Education and Experience:**

* 10+ years of precast concrete experience
* 5+ years production supervision or related experience

**Benefits:**

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Simple IRA with a Company Match
* Paid Time-off

Benefit Conditions:

* 60-Day waiting period
* Only full-time employees eligible

**Schedule:**

* Monday through Friday, minimum 45 hrs. Overtime & weekends may be required to meet project schedules.

**Pay Range:** Commensurate with experience

Plant Manager – Level 3 Water Treatment PlantNorth Greene Utilities (NGU)Baileyton, Tennessee

North Greene Utilities is seeking a certified Level 3 Water Treatment Plant Manager to lead operations at our Level 3 water treatment production plant in Baileyton Tennessee. This is a key leadership role responsible for the full management of plant functions, regulatory compliance, and a small team of operators.

Position Overview

The Plant Manager oversees all day-to-day and long-term operations of NGU’s Level 3 water treatment plant. The position ensures continuous production of safe, high-quality water that meets or exceeds all Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards and guidance. The manager supervises, mentors, and develops a team of three subordinates while maintaining efficient, safe, and compliant plant operations.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage all plant functions and treatment processes to meet TDEC and EPA regulatory requirements and policy guidance.• Supervise, mentor, and train three subordinates. Two subordinates are expected to achieve Level 1 certification by mid-2027.• Develop, implement, and manage shift schedules to ensure continuous, reliable plant coverage.• Ensure compliance with all federal and state safety regulations and NGU safety protocols.• Conduct lifecycle and operational management of treatment infrastructure, including maintenance planning and capital needs.• Participate in daily stand-up meetings with the NGU management team.• Assist with HR requirements for subordinates, including ensuring compliance with company policies.• Monitor the health and welfare of subordinates.• Conduct biannual performance counseling for subordinates.• Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to evolving operational requirements and tasks as directed by the Operations Supervisor and General Manager.• Maintain accurate records, reporting, and documentation required for regulatory compliance and internal management.

Qualifications

* Current Tennessee Level 3 Water Treatment Operator certification (required).• Proven experience in water treatment plant operations, preferably in a leadership or supervisory role.• Strong knowledge of TDEC and EPA drinking water regulations, treatment processes, and compliance requirements.• Ability to supervise, train, and develop staff.• Valid driver’s license and ability to meet any additional job-related certifications or requirements (e.g., safety, drug and alcohol screening).• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.• Commitment to safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.

Compensation and Benefits

NGU offers very competitive wages, an IRA, health insurance, and dental coverage. Additional details on pay and benefits will be discussed with qualified candidates.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume, copy of current Level 3 certification, and contact information to .

For questions, contact the office at 423-234-3145.

North Greene Utilities is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing reliable water service to our customers while supporting the professional growth of our team.

Pay: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

**Job Summary**
---------------

**Fresh & Ready Foods** is seeking a strategic and hands-on **Operations Director** to lead our Longview, TX manufacturing facility. As the site leader, this role is responsible for overseeing all aspects of production, food safety, quality, maintenance, warehousing, and distribution while driving operational excellence and developing high-performing teams.

Reporting to the Regional Director, the Operations Director will be accountable for achieving safety, quality, service, inventory, and financial objectives while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and employee engagement. This highly visible leadership role requires a strong manufacturing background, a passion for people development, and the ability to drive results in a fast-paced food production environment.

#### 

#### **Key Responsibilities**

* Provide overall leadership for plant operations, including production, quality, food safety, maintenance, warehousing, and distribution.
* Lead and develop managers, supervisors, and frontline teams to create a strong culture of accountability, engagement, and performance.
* Champion safety, regulatory compliance, and food safety programs, including SQF, HACCP, sanitation, and audit readiness.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to improve productivity, reduce waste, and optimize plant performance.
* Establish and manage KPIs related to safety, quality, labor, yield, inventory, customer service, and on-time delivery.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to support customer growth, new product introductions, and operational initiatives.
* Manage budgets, labor costs, inventory levels, and operational expenses to achieve financial objectives.
* Maintain a visible presence on the production floor, coaching leaders and supporting problem-solving efforts.
* Build succession plans and develop future leaders within the organization.
* Foster a culture focused on operational excellence, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement.

#### 

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations, Engineering, Business, Food Science, Supply Chain, or related field preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive leadership experience in food manufacturing, beverage manufacturing, CPG, protein processing, bakery, prepared foods, or related manufacturing environments.
* Experience managing large production teams through multiple levels of leadership.
* Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, Six Sigma, TPS, or similar methodologies.
* Proven track record improving safety, quality, productivity, and financial performance.
* Experience with SQF, HACCP, FDA/USDA regulations, sanitation programs, and quality systems.
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, labor management, inventory control, and operational reporting.
* Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership skills.

#### 

#### **Ideal Candidate**

The ideal candidate is a visible, people-focused manufacturing leader who enjoys building teams, developing talent, and driving operational results. They possess strong food manufacturing experience, a continuous improvement mindset, and a proven ability to lead large-scale operations while improving safety, quality, service, and profitability. Experience in high-volume food production environments is strongly preferred.

Braun Medical, visit www.bbraunusa.com

Ready to lead where science, quality, and patient safety come together? Join B. Braun and shape the future of laboratory excellence while driving the strategy, compliance, and innovation behind critical healthcare products.

**Why this role matters:**

The Director, Lab Quality Control serves as the senior site authority for Quality Control Chemistry and Microbiology, providing the scientific and operational leadership needed to protect product quality and maintain regulatory compliance. This role establishes the site’s laboratory strategy, leads critical quality initiatives, and ensures that laboratory operations remain scientifically sound, inspection-ready, and aligned with business and product portfolio requirements.

**How you will make an impact:**

* Develop, maintain, and execute the site Quality Control strategy in alignment with business objectives, product portfolio requirements, and regulatory expectations.
* Provide strategic oversight for QC Chemistry and QC Microbiology operations, including release, stability, raw material, in-process, microbiological, and sterility-related testing activities.
* Establish and govern laboratory standards for testing compliance, data integrity, investigations, sample management, analytical methods, specifications, and laboratory workflows.
* Serve as the primary site subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and customer audits involving laboratory operations and quality systems.
* Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Sterility Assurance, Engineering, Validation, Technical Services, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs to support site operations and timely product release.
* Lead laboratory optimization, method modernization, automation, Lean deployment, and quality system improvement initiatives.
* Foster a culture of quality, accountability, scientific rigor, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

**What sets you up for success:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline required; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.
* 10+ years of related experience, including significant leadership responsibility within laboratory quality control or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Demonstrated expertise in QC Chemistry and/or QC Microbiology operations within a sterile drug product manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience with laboratory compliance, data integrity, out-of-specification and out-of-trend investigations, analytical methods, and pharmaceutical quality systems.
* Proven experience supporting regulatory inspections, customer audits, and interactions with senior internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to resolve complex scientific, operational, and compliance issues using sound judgment, technical expertise, and risk-based decision-making.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated experience applying Lean and continuous-improvement methodologies preferred.

**What you will enjoy along the way:**

* The opportunity to shape the laboratory quality strategy for a regulated sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site.
* A highly visible leadership role with influence across Quality, Manufacturing, Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs.
* The ability to modernize analytical capabilities through automation, method lifecycle management, Lean principles, and emerging technologies.
* Responsibility for developing laboratory leaders, building organizational capability, and determining the effective allocation of people and resources.
* Meaningful work that directly supports product quality, regulatory compliance, operational reliability, and patient safety.
* A collaborative environment built on scientific rigor, accountability, diverse perspectives, and continuous improvement.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality
existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Region 1 $226,000-$266,000
 
Region 2 $MIN- $MID
 
Region 3 $MIN- $MID

A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Disclaimer: Beware of fake job offers!
 
We’ve been alerted to scammers posing as ŌURA recruiters, especially for remote roles. Please note:

* Our jobs are listed only on the ŌURA Careers page and trusted job boards.
* We will never ask for personal information like ID or payment for equipment upfront.
* Official offers are sent through Docusign after a verbal offer, not via text or email.

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

To all recruitment agencies: ŌURA does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ŌURA employees, or any other organization's location. ŌURA is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality Systems and Compliance
existing_roles.description:
Apnimed is a rapidly growing pharmaceutical company working to transform the treatment of sleep apnea based on a simple idea – patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) could benefit from treatment with a safe and effective oral medication dosed once daily at bedtime. Our lead development program, AD109, targets the neurologic control of upper airway muscles to maintain an open airway during sleep. Apnimed is committed to innovation, as well as state-of-the-art advancements in sleep medicine, which is leading to the development of a portfolio of novel pharmacologic therapies for sleep apnea and related disorders.

Recognized by the Boston Business Journal as one of the Best Places to Work in both 2024 and 2025, we are continuing to grow and build the foundational operations that enable our employees and our mission to thrive.

**Summary**:

The Senior Manager, Quality Systems & Compliance reports to the Senior Director, GCP Quality Assurance and Quality Compliance and is responsible for administering, maintaining, and continuously improving Apnimed's electronic Quality Management System (eQMS) and associated quality processes, and for keeping them inspection-ready. The successful candidate will also play a key role in strengthening the Quality Management System infrastructure as a business partner across GxP and corporate quality functions, ensuring quality processes remain compliant, scalable, and aligned with the company's transition toward commercialization. This is an exciting opportunity to strengthen the quality infrastructure that supports Apnimed as part of a major paradigm shift in the treatment of sleep apnea from medical devices and surgery to a first in class pharmaceutical treatment.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $170,000.00 to $190,000.00. Final compensation will depend on the selected candidate’s level, education and relevant experience.

### **Key Job Duties include, but are not limited to:**

* Serve as subject matter expert and administrator for the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), evaluating proposed system changes and coordinating testing, validation, and deployment activities.
* Support the integration of new business processes, departments, and vendors into the Quality Management System, and oversee onboarding, knowledge transfer, and competency requirements for new eQMS administrators.
* Maintain system documentation, including procedures, work instructions, validation documentation, and configuration records.
* Administer the training program: confirm assignments and curricula reflect quality system responsibilities, manage role-based eQMS training and user support, and maintain a centralized library of user guidance, job aids, and FAQs.
* Provide oversight and support for core quality processes, including document control, deviations, CAPAs, change controls, investigations, supplier quality records, and training management.
* Manage vendor governance activities and periodic performance reviews, ensuring reviews are completed and properly documented and filed.
* Keep quality systems and records in a state of continuous inspection readiness; support regulatory inspections and audits through preparation of records, reports, metrics, and system demonstrations; and monitor industry trends and regulatory expectations.
* Present quality system performance trends and recommendations to Quality leadership, lead or support continuous improvement initiatives, and collaborate cross-functionally to standardize quality processes across departments.

 
**Requirements** 

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent in a scientific, technical, engineering, quality, or related discipline.
* 8+ years of Quality Assurance, Quality Systems, or Quality Management experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or life sciences industry, including:
* Demonstrated experience managing electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS), including administering or supporting platforms such as Dot Compliance, Veeva Quality, MasterControl, TrackWise Digital, ComplianceWire, or similar.
* Working knowledge of FDA, EMA, ICH, GCP, GMP, and GLP requirements.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and external/internal audits.
* Preferred: Direct administrator experience with Veeva Quality, and experience with computerized system validation (CSV) and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.
* Preferred: Experience supporting both development-stage and commercial pharmaceutical operations, and implementing or enhancing eQMS platforms.
* Ability to manage simultaneous priorities and changing deadlines.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills.
* Proficiency in the use of MS Word, PowerPoint; experience with Adobe Acrobat Professional.

 
**Benefits** 

* 401(k) with company match
* Generous time off for vacation
* Generous healthcare benefits
* Flexible working environment
* Motivated and experienced team
* Winner of 2024 and 2025 Boston Business Journal Best Places to Work

### **Location and Other Information:**

* Apnimed is a publicly licensed company based in Cambridge, MA; we are generally virtual and specific location within the US is not critical.
* We are a small growing Company with an inclusive environment.
* Must be able to travel as necessary.
* Apnimed is an EEO employer committed to an exciting, diverse, and enriching work environment.
* Please visit us at www.apnimed.com to learn more about our work with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler (MC) is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber's first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

### **About The Role:**

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Platform Manufacturing Engineering to lead Production Manufacturing Engineering as we scale the Matter Compiler from pilot production into high-volume manufacturing. You will own the equipment that builds our devices — its build, integration, bring-up, qualification and reliability — and the team of engineers who deliver it.

**You are an engineer first.** This is a player-coach role and the player half is not decorative: you will spearhead the hardest projects on the critical path personally, in CAD and on the floor, and use that work as the vehicle for coaching everyone around you. The fastest way to set a standard here is to define it while you produce work that meets it, then mentor your team to achieve the same bar.

Mentoring here happens inside the work, not alongside it. You will pull engineers onto the projects you lead, hand off scope as they are ready for it, review their designs with real technical depth, and grow the next set of project leads out of people who learned by building with you.

The management half is real. You will hire against a plan rather than a wish list, develop engineers toward the next level, run performance honestly, and install the operating standards this function works to — documentation, change control, qualification and release discipline, and what "done" means before work leaves the group. You will plan the organization ahead of where the business is today, own headcount and capital budget, and get manufacturability and equipment requirements into specifications set by other teams rather than reviewing them at the end.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Spearhead the hardest equipment projects on the critical path yourself — architecture, CAD, build, bring-up and qualification — and bring engineers along on them as the primary way they develop.
* Lead a team of 5–10 engineers spanning equipment design, automation and controls, integration, and sustaining, through a mix of direct reports and technical leads.
* Set the engineering standard by producing work to it: reference designs, qualification plans, RCCAs and documentation your team can pattern from, with the reasoning made explicit so it transfers.
* Coach through the work — pair on designs, run technical reviews with real depth, hand off scope as engineers are ready for it, and grow the next set of project leads out of people who built alongside you.
* Own the delivery record for the function — the equipment, qualifications and production readiness your team commits to, against committed dates.
* Lead equipment deployment end to end: installation, validation, commissioning, acceptance testing, SOP/WI release and operator qualification.
* Run root cause and corrective action personally on the failures that matter, teach the method by doing it in front of the team, and drive the corrective actions across teams that do not report to you.
* Install and uphold the operating standards: documentation, change control, qualification and release discipline, RCCA method and closure, and how work is reviewed before it leaves the group.
* Plan organizational growth — forecast hiring needs ahead of demand, define roles and levels, build and defend the hiring plan, and manage headcount and capital budget with Supply Chain and Finance.
* Own and resolve escalated personnel situations arising from business and priority changes, rather than routing them away.
* Get manufacturability and equipment requirements into specification setting and design milestones with Design Engineering and Product, rather than reviewing at the end.
* Balance competing priorities with peer leaders so committed deliverables are still met, and own communication of impact and resolution path where they cannot be.
* Own contract manufacturer and automation supplier execution through final integration and test to conformant hardware on schedule.
* Drive throughput, yield, cost and uptime improvement — held with control limits, not delivered as one-time gains — and establish the operating metrics and reporting cadence leadership can rely on without chasing.
* Travel between Emeryville and Santa Clara sites as needed.

### **What You'll Need:**

* 7+ years of manufacturing or equipment engineering experience, including 3+ years managing engineers with 5 or more direct reports.
* **Current hands-on capability.** You still design in CAD, still debug hardware on the floor, and could take the hardest open task on your team's board tomorrow. We will test this directly in the loop.
* Proven ownership of automated production equipment end to end — architecture through mechanical, controls and software integration, into a qualified, released system running in production.
* Proficiency in CAD for equipment design (SolidWorks, Onshape, AutoCAD or similar), with recent personal use.
* A track record of **developing engineers through the work** — specific people who grew because you put them on projects you were leading, reviewed their designs, and handed off scope as they were ready for it.
* A track record of building out a functional group: defining roles, hiring against a plan, and installing the operating standards — not only inheriting an existing team.
* Experience leading a team spanning more than one discipline (e.g., equipment, controls/automation, integration, sustaining), including people whose work sits outside your own background.
* Ownership of headcount and capital budget, with resourcing tradeoff decisions made under real constraint.
* Depth across DFx, RCCA, eBOMmBOM conversion, qualification and acceptance testing, and PLM/document control and release (Arena a plus).
* Experience in semiconductor, solar, hardware-based biotech, EV, or similar high-tech industries.
* Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functionally without authority — specifically, getting manufacturing and equipment requirements into specifications owned by other teams.
* A first-principles mindset — you question assumptions, reframe problems from the ground up, and approach challenges with a foundational understanding rather than relying solely on precedent.
* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

### **Bonus Points For:**

* Experience standing up or rebuilding a manufacturing or equipment engineering function at a company moving from pilot to production scale.
* Experience staying technically current while managing — a design, patent, or build you personally delivered while running a team.
* Knowledge of basic coding: RSLogix, Ignition, Python, or C/C++.

Atomic Machines is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and does not discriminate based on characteristics protected by applicable law. We are committed to an inclusive interview experience, including for individuals with disabilities. To request an accommodation, contact rc@atomicmachines.com. To help our recruiting team manage application volume and respond to candidates more efficiently, Atomic Machines may use AI-assisted tools.

existing_roles.title: Manager / Senior Manager, Technical Operations
existing_roles.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with **neffy®**, the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you're motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

 

The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).
* Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.
* Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.
* Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.
* Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.
* Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.
* Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.
* Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.
* Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.
* Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.
* Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.
* Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.
* Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.
* Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:**

* Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.
* Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.
* Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.
* Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.
* Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.
* Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor's degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree is a plus. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.
* Minimum of 5 years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process/formulation development, CMC, supply chain, or a related function.
* Experience working with external CMOs/CDMOs and supporting GMP clinical and/or commercial manufacturing is strongly preferred.
* Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.
* Experience reviewing manufacturing batch records and process documentation and supporting technical investigations, change controls, and regulatory CMC activities is preferred.
* Experience supporting commercial distribution/3PL operations, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and/or clinical supply and IRT/IWRS activities is preferred.

Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering - Centralia, MO
existing_roles.description:
**Job Overview**
----------------

The Senior Manufacturing Engineering Manager is responsible for overseeing and leading a team of engineers to deliver technical projects efficiently and effectively. This role involves managing resources, budgets, and project timelines, ensuring high-quality engineering solutions, and providing technical guidance. The Senior Manufacturing Engineering Manager is responsible for team development, stakeholder communication and implementing best practices to achieve project goals and drive innovation. 
#LI-BB2

**A Day In The Life**
---------------------

Every day at Hubbell is different and you’ll contribute in many ways. On any given day, you’ll make a difference by:

Serving in a leadership role, directly supervising project engineers and designers.

Overseeing, managing, and supporting calibration programs for the facilities, including production equipment, facility equipment.

Developing concepts for new and revised products maximizing function, safety, features, and user benefits while minimizing costs.

Directing preparation of models and lab testing as required to develop product.

Preparing and maintaining Project Control Charts and schedules.

Participating in meetings as required to communicate and coordinate projects with various departments within Hubbell.

Developing the site maintenance budget for approval and managing site budget costs to meet the approved budget targets.

Directing preparation of product drawings and checking completed drawings.

Preparing product standards and specifications and obtaining agency listings as required (UL/CSA etc.).

Approving tooling, assemblies, and updating drawings. Release approved product for production.

**What will help you thrive in this role?**
-------------------------------------------

Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (required)

10+ years of relevant experience (required)

5+ supervisory experience in an engineering related field (required)

Ability to check design drawings with extreme thoroughness while paying strict attention to detail

Ability to manage multiple design projects with varying priority levels

Proven track record working with systems engineering functions including concept of operations development, requirements management, technical risk management, interface definition and control

Experience effectively communicating and presenting with all levels of management and individual contributors on the program team

Strong organization, coordination, planning and collaboration skills

Experience supporting engineering teams in a multi-discipline environment

Experience conducting system integration and system tests to include development of integration and test plans, test cases and procedures

Ability to visualize system functionality, to create block diagrams, and to analyze system performance

**Hubbell Incorporated**

Hubbell creates critical infrastructure solutions that power our customers, communities, people and the planet. Our company is strategically aligned around enabling grid modernization and electrification. As more products plug in to an aging grid, Hubbell solutions enable the transition to a more reliable, resilient and efficient energy infrastructure. Founded in 1888 our innovation has made us a leading global manufacturer of high quality electrical and utility solutions enabling customers to operate critical infrastructure reliably and efficiently.

The company operates in two segments.
